newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Foreign criminals threaten Vietnam, warns journal.
newsitem.headline: Foreign criminals threaten Vietnam, warns journal.

text.p: An official newspaper warned on Wednesday that foreign criminals were taking advantage of Vietnam's open-door policy, and called for tightened controls on overseas visitors and residents.

A lengthy article in the Phap Luat (Law) journal catalogued a range of crimes committed over the past 18 months by foreigners in Vietnam, including drugs trafficking, arms smuggling, robbery and murder.
It said 54 cases involving 74 foreign defendants had been tried in 21 out of Vietnam's 61 People's Courts.
Some of those cases involved supplying children and women to brothels in Macau, Hong Kong, Singapore, China and Cambodia, while others involved the circulation of counterfeit money, it said.
"Is that part of a plot to sabotage Vietnam's social and economic reforms, to make Vietnam weaker in the post-war era?" it asked rhetorically.

The article went on to call for tightened border controls, closer supervision of residency permits issued to foreigners and increased cooperation between Vietnam's security authorities and those in other countries.
Wednesday's article was the latest of several recently to warn about the dangers posed to Vietnam by the activities of foreigners in a number of areas, including business.
Analysts say they are linked to internal political jostling among groups vying for influence ahead of a planned leadership change which is due to be announced in September.
Vietnam introduced economic reform and open-door policies in the late 1980s in place of a closed Soviet-style system.

The policies are generally seen as having been successful, but conservative groups have pointed to problems such as growing social vice and the threat of subversion as evidence of a need for a strengthening of national security mechanisms.
